correctness.rationale: The universally quantified two-input graph-variation constant follows by (i) a rigorous support-reduction proof that maximal covariance of two fixed finite signals over all probability vectors equals one quarter of the maximum nonnegative concordant pair product, (ii) duality on the quotient by constants for the softmax Jacobian, (iii) coarea/min-cut identification of the graph variation dual difference norm, and (iv) Jacobian integration plus limiting two-atom inputs for sharpness. A bridge argument proves the global n/4 envelope and identifies its equality cases; standard local connectivity counts give the tree and complete-bipartite corollaries. The code computes 240570 covariance tests, 1547790 unweighted cut/Jacobian tests across 771 connected labelled graphs, 30308 weighted tests, 14 rational star limiting witnesses, and 15 biclique parameter checks. These finite checks are corroboration and not the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies an exact, naturally motivated perturbation-stability invariant for graph probability signals and gives a general weighted minimum-cut formula for all finite connected graphs. The nonexpansivity condition is necessary and sufficient and computable from graph cuts. In the unweighted case it gives a sharp n/4 envelope and identifies every extremizing graph, fully classifies stable trees and gives a sharp biclique imbalance threshold. This qualitatively separates standard ell-p softmax contraction from potentially growing graph-variation amplification; the theorem is neither a routine substitution nor an arbitrary finite numerical instance.
